title: Case: Pallet delivery lacks a receiving-dock appointment
context: The pallet is booked for a business consignee whose warehouse requires a receiving-dock appointment. Carrier and consignee must use the same reference and time.
initial_request: Please book with authorised receiving coordinator Ossa Rell. Obtain the dock reference, time and receiving entrance for our driver.

events.body:
Pallet DL-3625 for Arcloom Components has no receiving appointment. We can reach its dock on 2027-03-14 afternoon, but will not send the truck without a consignee appointment.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-165.txt
Please book with authorised receiving coordinator Ossa Rell. Obtain the dock reference, time and receiving entrance for our driver.
Please book with authorised receiving coordinator Ossa Rell. Obtain the dock reference, time and receiving entrance for our driver.

attachments.name: label-scan-165.txt
attachments.text:
LABEL SCAN
Shipment: DL-20005
Consignee: Orla Quarrie
Address: 51 Copse Lane
Status at scan: DELIVERED, left in safe place
Scanned: 2027-03-13T09:00:00Z

acceptable_actions.summary: Contact the consignee's receiving coordinator to book an available dock slot.

must_not: An appointment reference establishes coordinated booking, not pallet receipt.
Treats label-scan-165.txt as evidence about DL-3625: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-20005)
Tells anyone that DL-3625 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-165.txt
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Please offer an available receiving-dock appointment for pallet DL-3625 on 2027-03-14 afternoon, with dock reference and entrance.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-041: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. label-scan-165.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-20005); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
